content.thinking:
I'm designing a frost-forged battle axe in League of Legends style, planning it mounted upright on an ice-crystal plinth with a haft around 1.4 meters and a large crescent blade, sized to real-world proportions.

I'll use a single root joint since the whole weapon is a rigid object with no articulation needed, then build the haft vertically and extrude the crescent blade forward using a coordinate system that defines its thickness along the X-axis.

Working out crescent blade outline coordinates...

Mapping out the full nine-point outline for the axe head with sharp corners at the tip points, checking it forms a convex, non-self-intersecting polygon before applying corner-cutting smoothing.

Now I'm planning the layering for the blade: an outer dark steel-blue rim extrude, a slightly thicker inset ice-light panel scaled toward the centroid to create a raised look, and a bright cyan edge strip along the bevel for highlight.

Working out the geometry for rune decal planes on the blade faces, figuring out thickness offsets and the local basis vectors so the plane aligns correctly against each face.

Still designing the rune texture...

Now for the haft, I'm planning a swept rod geometry with grain paint showing a leather-wrapped lower grip transitioning to dark steel, using banded gradient coloring along the sweep path.

Breaking the haft into bands by position: a steel cap near the top, a leather-wrapped section below with spiraling stripe texture, then frost-rune steel grain further down. I'm also planning lathed collar rings at several grip heights, and thinking through how the pommel end rests into a stacked ice plinth base.

Still writing the plinth geometry... octagonal lathe outline with mottled ice-stone paint, scattered glowing ice-shard cones around the base, and a steel ring; then shaping the box socket where the haft meets the axe head, plus flaring ornamental end caps.

I'm defining a color palette of navy steel, icy blues, cyan glow, and gold accents, then working out the blade geometry -- crisp rim edges, an inset gradient panel scaled toward the centroid, and preserving sharp corner points in the outline data.

Now I'm adding depth details: a beveled outer extrude paired with a thicker beveled inner panel, a swept beard/spike shape trailing behind the head, and a cone-shaped finial topping off the haft.

Rethinking proportions—1.8m felt too tall for a battle axe, so I'm rescaling everything by 0.8, adjusting the haft to run roughly 0.12 to 1.32, repositioning the blade center, and recalculating the outline's vertical span accordingly.

Still working out the exact dimensions for the head box, rune plane, and collar placements to finalize a ~1.6m total height with proportional parts.

Now I'm defining the haft length and the colored bands along it, placing navy, leather-paint, and steel-paint segments at specific points to mark the grip and collars, then starting to work out a spiral ribbon wrap for the lower hand-grip using a parametric spiral function.

I'm also planning small swallowtail cloth ribbons hanging near the haft head, deciding where to position them along the axis and which plane to extrude them in.

I'll hang this shape below the head box with a cyan-to-navy gradient and a gold bead on top, then add gold rivet spheres merged onto the box geometry near the bone root, followed by ice crystal clusters near the blade root using octahedron and cone shapes.

Adding more crystal cones...

Wrapping colors with cel for a toon shading look, keeping glow-eligible parts as plain strings, and trimming imports to just what's used (cel, INK, plus gradient/grain/stripes/mottle from paint, and rng for shard variation). Now sketching the rune SVG with a 64x96 viewbox.

Writing SVG paths...

Still refining blade geometry...

I'm defining a helper to convert u,v coordinates into model space, then adding plinth details with a mottled stone-and-paint texture plus a steel ring at the haft base. I'm also planning small gold wing extrudes near the socket as a crossguard-like accent.

Now I'm writing a crystal-shard helper that builds a cone geometry oriented along a direction vector, with optional glow, and attaching it to the nearest joint when no bone is specified. Setting up the ring of shards...

Placing small glowing octahedron gems on the box sides, then sweeping the haft geometry from the base up to the top with an 8-sided flat-capped profile, checking it fits within the box width. Setting the head box to a navy color, cleaning up unused imports, and writing the final file.
